questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Show other drivers that you are angry.
Alert other drivers that you are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others that you are there. Since the horn can startle drivers and cause danger, only use it when needed.

questions.question: When driving down a long hill, you should brake by:

options.text: Using mostly brakes and sometimes downshifting.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Before going down a long hill, shift to a lower gear and then brake properly. Using only brakes can make them too hot and fail. The engine's braking power works best in a lower gear to control your speed going downhill.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.explanation: Check your vehicle's gauges before you drive. After starting the engine, the coolant temperature should slowly increase to normal operating range.

questions.question: Over-the-counter medication:

options.text: Is safe for drivers and poses no risks.
Is not covered by any driving under the influence laws.
Can make it harder for you to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make it harder for you to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can have side effects that affect your driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any controlled substance, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is almost at idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle.
questions.explanation: To stop smoothly, press the brake pedal slowly and gently. For manual transmission vehicles, push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Use only brakes to slow down.

questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and downshift before going down the hill. Using only brakes can make them too hot and less effective.

questions.question: Which vehicle does NOT get an exemption from needing a CDL?
questions.explanation: Under certain conditions, you do not need a CDL to drive military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. You also do not need a CDL for a straight truck carrying only your personal belongings that you are not selling.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is better because:

options.text: The driver can see the back of the vehicle best.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see the back of the vehicle best.
questions.explanation: When driving in reverse, always back your vehicle to the left side. This gives you the best view of the rear of your vehicle.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing has no warning gates or lights, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are probably abandoned.
Stop and walk to the tracks to see if a train is coming.
Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
Do what the other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look down the tracks in both directions to check for trains.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you need to:

options.text: Park your vehicle on an uphill slope.
Park your vehicle on a downhill slope.

questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle under control. It also gives other drivers time to move out of your way if you did not see them. Always use a turn signal to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, how should it be?
questions.explanation: Check the exhaust system to make sure no parts are loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: When should you watch for black ice?

options.text: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin layer of clear ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must identify all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for damage or wear. If any of these are not belt-driven, tell the examiner which ones. Verify that all parts work properly, are mounted securely, and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: What may you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset backing, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It takes your attention and your hands off the road.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your attention and your hands off the road.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts your mind from the road and takes at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How quickly you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Do not cause an accident or break any traffic laws.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other rests.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle approaches a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following is not part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, air storage tanks, gauges, a low air pressure warning signal, foundation brakes, and spring brakes. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what is important to do?

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Place the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how the cargo's weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Each axle should carry the right amount of weight—not too little and not too much. Incorrect loading can affect steering, reduce tire grip, and damage the axles.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must keep ____ in contact with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If you are exiting a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down, you should:

options.text: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the driver's window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Before you slow down, tap your brake pedal lightly a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: If your vehicle skids from pressing the accelerator too hard, you should:

options.text: Remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: A skid from pressing the accelerator too hard can be fixed by taking your foot off the accelerator. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead. This gives you more room to make safe moves and gives the tailgater a chance to pass. Do not speed up when being tailgated, as the other driver may just follow you more closely at the higher speed, making the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, you need a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, your vehicle's speed will likely:

options.text: Match the speed of other traffic

questions.explanation: Gravity will cause your vehicle to go faster when driving downhill. Before going down a hill, choose a safe speed for your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Crashes caused by tired drivers happen most often at night.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
The total weight of a vehicle's tractor only
The total weight of a loaded trailer only
The weight of a tractor and trailer without the load

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle including everything it is carrying.

questions.question: What shows you how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Cause some of the brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some of the brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment will wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: How often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator in cold weather?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from building up in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and makes a loud bang, when does the truck feel the effect?

options.text: Only if the damaged tire is at the front of the truck.
Only if the truck is carrying a load.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay between when a tire fails and when you feel it affect the truck. This delay may make you think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: Where should regrooved tires NOT be used?

options.text: On the front wheels of a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do first?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Do not use gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank. Wear gloves or use a cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: Why are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions give you extra gears. They are usually controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when crossing railroad tracks during a driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are called "headache racks." They protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles that have this valve, a lever on the dashboard controls it.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So that it must be backed up to leave the space.
So that it can be pulled forward to leave the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that it can be pulled forward to leave the space.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while you are driving:

options.text: Allows air to reach the cargo and keep it cool.

questions.explanation: A cargo cover should not flap while you are driving. It could tear loose and uncover the cargo. It might also block your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning light comes on if air pressure falls below 60 psi. Some vehicles use a wig wag signal instead.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should always steer to the left.
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
You should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may help you avoid a hazard. Shoulders are usually strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: If you hear or feel something unusual while driving, you should:

options.text: Assume it is not a concern and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle makes it until another driver takes over.
Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you notice anything unusual—a strange sound, smell, or feeling—stop and check the vehicle to find the cause.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, you apply the parking brake by using:
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, a diamond-shaped yellow knob controls the parking brake. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed only on the left side, if possible.
Placed only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in a trailer. If weight is too high, the vehicle may tip over.
